title: Robust Nonparametric Confidence Intervals for Regression-Discontinuity Designs
research_question: How can researchers obtain confidence intervals for treatment effects at a known assignment cutoff that remain valid and exhibit close-to-correct empirical coverage even when the bandwidth used to localize estimation around the cutoff is relatively large? Specifically, how should inference about average treatment effects at the threshold be conducted in sharp, sharp kink, fuzzy, and fuzzy kink threshold-based assignment settings so that coverage does not deteriorate due to bias from data-driven bandwidth choices?
data_description: The paper is primarily methodological and theoretical, with empirical content provided through a Monte Carlo simulation study and a supplemental empirical illustration. The simulation generates 5,000 replications of samples of size n = 500, with a running variable drawn as X_i ~ 2·Beta(2,4) − 1 and an additive Gaussian error with standard deviation 0.1295. Three regression functions are studied: two are calibrated to actual datasets used in prior applied work — Lee (2008) on U.S. House elections and Ludwig and Miller (2007) on Head Start — and a third is constructed to display greater curvature. The supplemental empirical application uses household-level data from the Mexican Progresa/Oportunidades conditional cash transfer program. Companion R and STATA software packages implement the procedures. Key quantities include the outcome, a continuous score/forcing variable, and (in fuzzy settings) a binary treatment indicator.
institutional_context: The motivating setting is one in which units are assigned to a treatment based on whether an observed continuous score crosses a known threshold, with the probability of treatment changing sharply at that cutoff. Classic examples include scholarship awards granted to students whose test scores exceed a fixed level (Thistlethwaite and Campbell, 1960), close electoral races where winning depends on crossing a vote-share threshold, and social programs such as Head Start or Progresa/Oportunidades whose eligibility depends on a poverty or need index. Variants include settings where treatment intensity changes slope rather than level at the cutoff (kink settings), and settings where actual treatment receipt only partially follows the assignment rule (fuzzy settings). Such threshold-based assignment rules are widely used across economics, political science, and education as quasi-experimental sources of variation.
